definition: Elements of AI is a massive open online course (MOOC) teaching the basics of artificial intelligence.
details: The course, originally launched in 2018, is designed and organized by the University of Helsinki and learning technology company MinnaLearn. The course includes modules on machine learning, neural networks, the philosophy of artificial intelligence, and using artificial intelligence to solve problems. It consists of two parts: Introduction to AI and its sequel, Building AI, that was released in late 2020. In November 2019, the course was named one of four winners of MIT’s Inclusive Innovation Challenge. University of Helsinki's computer science department is known as the alma mater of Linus Torvalds, a Finnish-American software engineer who is the creator of the Linux kernel, which is the kernel for Linux operating systems.

explainer.lead: Elements of AI is a free-form online course format for learning what artificial intelligence is and how it can be used. Created by the University of Helsinki and MinnaLearn, it gives beginners a structured route through core ideas before moving on to building with AI.

tiers.eli5: Elements of AI is like a two-part beginner's guide to smart computer systems. The first part introduces the main ideas, and the second part, Building AI, takes learners further. It covers topics such as how computers learn, neural networks, and what AI means for people.
tiers.practitioner: An engineer can use Elements of AI as a structured introduction to machine learning, neural networks, AI philosophy, and problem-solving with AI. The natural starting point is Introduction to AI, followed by its sequel, Building AI. The course should not be confused with a software framework or assumed to provide production-engineering experience by itself.
tiers.paperLevel: Elements of AI is a two-part massive open online course comprising Introduction to AI and Building AI. Its curriculum covers machine learning, neural networks, the philosophy of artificial intelligence, and the use of AI to solve problems. The original course launched in 2018, and Building AI was released in late 2020.

explainer.example: A beginner completes Introduction to AI, studies its neural-networks module, and learns how AI can be applied to problems. They then continue to Building AI for the second part of the learning path.
explainer.intuition: The course turns a broad, technical subject into a two-stage learning path: first understand the central ideas, then move toward building with AI.
howItWorks: Begin with Introduction to AI, the original course launched in 2018.
Study introductory topics including machine learning and neural networks.
Explore the philosophy of artificial intelligence alongside the technical material.
Learn about using artificial intelligence to solve problems.
Continue with Building AI, the sequel released in late 2020.
explainer.whyItMatters: It offers an organized entry point into both the technical and philosophical sides of AI. Its recognition as one of four winners of MIT's Inclusive Innovation Challenge in November 2019 also marked its broader educational impact.
misconceptions: It is a MOOC, not an AI model, algorithm, or software library.
Building AI is the sequel released in late 2020, not the original 2018 course.
Linus Torvalds's connection is to the University of Helsinki's computer science department, not to authorship of the course.
